note: CKEditor 5 Icons contributes exactly one CKEditor 5 plugin, `ckeditor5_icons_icon` (toolbar button id `icon`, label 'Icons'). It has NO configure route, no settings form, no permissions, no Drush commands and no plugin types of its own. All of its persistent state lives per text format inside editor.editor.<format>: the `icon` entry in settings.toolbar.items plus settings.plugins.ckeditor5_icons_icon with keys fa_version ('6'|'5'), fa_styles (subset of solid/regular/light/thin/duotone/brands/custom), custom_metadata, async_metadata, recommended_enabled and recommended_icons — validated by the schema ckeditor5.plugin.ckeditor5_icons_icon. Font Awesome metadata for 6.7.2 and 5.15.4 ships inside the module (libraries/fontawesome{5,6}/metadata) and is served through three CSRF-protected routes registered by MetadataRouting at /modules/contrib/ckeditor5_icons/metadata/fontawesome{6,5,}. Every medium/hard case is grounded in that real editor.editor config; all scripts create and delete text formats namespaced `ckeditor5_icons_*` so they cannot collide with the site's shared formats.

evals.prompt: I installed the Drupal contrib module ckeditor5_icons on a Drupal 11 site but I cannot find an admin settings page for it. How do I actually turn the Font Awesome icon picker on, and where is that choice stored in configuration?
evals.expected_output: There is no configure route and no global settings form. You configure it per text format: go to Configuration -> Content authoring -> Text formats and editors (/admin/config/content/formats), Configure the format, drag the 'Icons' button into the CKEditor 5 toolbar, then use the 'Icons' vertical tab. It is stored in editor.editor.<format>: 'icon' in settings.toolbar.items and the keys under settings.plugins.ckeditor5_icons_icon (fa_version, fa_styles, custom_metadata, async_metadata, recommended_enabled, recommended_icons).

evals.prompt: In a Drupal site's exported configuration, which config object and which keys does the ckeditor5_icons module use to record the Font Awesome version and the enabled icon styles for a text format? Give the plugin id and the key names.
evals.expected_output: The CKEditor 5 plugin id is ckeditor5_icons_icon and its settings live in editor.editor.<format> under settings.plugins.ckeditor5_icons_icon. Keys: fa_version ('6' or '5'), fa_styles (a sequence of style names), custom_metadata, async_metadata, recommended_enabled and recommended_icons. The schema is ckeditor5.plugin.ckeditor5_icons_icon.

evals.prompt: When an editor inserts an icon with the Drupal ckeditor5_icons module, what HTML does it put in the body field, and does the module itself load the Font Awesome stylesheet on the front end?
evals.expected_output: It inserts a plain element carrying Font Awesome classes, e.g. (Font Awesome 5 uses fas/far/fab instead of fa-solid/fa-regular/fa-brands). The plugin declares and as allowed elements so restricted formats keep them. The module does NOT load the Font Awesome CSS/webfont on the front end - it only ships icon metadata and the picker, so the library must already be provided by the theme, a CDN include or the fontawesome contrib module.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a text format whose machine name starts with ckeditor5_icons. Inspect the live configuration and tell me which major version of Font Awesome its ckeditor5_icons icon picker is configured for, and which icon names are listed in its Recommended category.
evals.expected_output: The format is ckeditor5_icons_eval. Reading editor.editor.ckeditor5_icons_eval -> settings.plugins.ckeditor5_icons_icon shows fa_version: '5' (Font Awesome 5) and recommended_icons: [drupal, heart, star] with recommended_enabled: true (async_metadata is false, fa_styles are solid and brands).

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has two text formats, ckeditor5_icons_alpha and ckeditor5_icons_beta, and both have the ckeditor5_icons Icons button in their CKEditor 5 toolbar. Exactly one of them restricts the icon picker to Font Awesome brand icons only. Inspect the live configuration and tell me which format that is.
evals.expected_output: ckeditor5_icons_beta. Its editor.editor.ckeditor5_icons_beta -> settings.plugins.ckeditor5_icons_icon.fa_styles is [brands], whereas ckeditor5_icons_alpha has [solid, regular, brands].

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a text format with the machine name ckeditor5_icons_task that uses CKEditor 5 but has no icon picker. Using the ckeditor5_icons module, add its Icons button to that format's toolbar and configure the plugin for Font Awesome 6 with the Solid, Regular and Brands styles enabled, the Recommended category turned on, and exactly the icons drupal and heart listed as recommended. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: editor.editor.ckeditor5_icons_task ends up with 'icon' in settings.toolbar.items and settings.plugins.ckeditor5_icons_icon = {fa_version: '6', fa_styles: [solid, regular, brands], custom_metadata: false, async_metadata: true, recommended_enabled: true, recommended_icons: [drupal, heart]} - set either through /admin/config/content/formats/manage/ckeditor5_icons_task or by loading the Editor entity and saving its settings.

evals.prompt: Our site still ships the older Font Awesome 5 stylesheet, but the icon picker on the text format called ckeditor5_icons_legacy is inserting icons that do not show up. Make that format's icon picker match Font Awesome 5, and while you are there let editors choose only the plain solid icons and the brand logos - drop the outline/regular style. Change it on the live site.
evals.expected_output: In editor.editor.ckeditor5_icons_legacy, settings.plugins.ckeditor5_icons_icon.fa_version becomes '5' and fa_styles becomes exactly [solid, brands] (the icons then emit FA5 class names fas/fab instead of fa-solid/fa-brands). The 'icon' toolbar item stays in settings.toolbar.items.
